---
title: "Lab · Greeting Capsule (Steps 1–3)"
---

The lab for this lesson is the shared
[**Greeting Capsule**](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/) lab. It
lives at the repository root so later Part 2 lessons can reuse the
same solution tree.

For Module 2 ("Define a capsule") only **Steps 1–3** of the
walkthrough are in scope: fetch the upstream artefacts, author
`solution/capsule.yaml` from memo1 §3, and validate it against the
upstream `capsule.schema.json`. Later modules pick up at Step 4
(implementation and tests) and Step 6 (compose the Pico).

## What this lab covers for Module 2

- [Step 1 — Fetch the upstream artefacts](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/walkthrough.html#step-1-fetch-the-upstream-artefacts)
  downloads the pinned
  [`capsule.schema.json`](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/capsule.schema.json)
  and the fixture set used by the exercise into the lab-local,
  untracked `build/upstream/` directory.
- [Step 2 — Write the capsule document](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/walkthrough.html#step-2-write-the-capsule-document)
  authors `solution/capsule.yaml` verbatim from
  [memo1 §3](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo1.md#3-worked-example-illustrative-not-valid-until-adopted-upstream)
  with the capability identifier conformed to memo2 §3 D3.
- [Step 3 — Validate it against the upstream schema](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/walkthrough.html#step-3-validate-it-against-the-upstream-schema)
  runs the JSON Schema 2020-12 validator against `capsule.yaml` and
  against one upstream invalid fixture, confirming the schema accepts
  the valid document and rejects the invalid one for the stated
  reason.

## Where to go

Open the [Greeting Capsule lab](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/)
and follow the walkthrough through the end of Step 3:

- [Objectives and prerequisites](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/objectives.html)
- [Walkthrough](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/walkthrough.html) —
  stop after Step 3 for this module.
- [Solution](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/solution.html) — the
  reference `solution/capsule.yaml` matches the capsule block in this
  lesson's [index](index.qmd#a-valid-minimal-capsule).

## What you will produce

By the end of Step 3 you will have:

- an untracked `labs/greeting-capsule/build/upstream/` directory
  holding the pinned `capsule.schema.json` and fixtures (never
  committed — the lab-local `.gitignore` excludes `build/`);
- `labs/greeting-capsule/solution/capsule.yaml`, which validates
  against the upstream schema;
- a confirmed rejection of one upstream invalid fixture with the
  error message named in its `# fails:` comment.

That evidence satisfies memo23 §4 Module 2 ("a valid capsule
definition and contract tests or validation rules") at the
contract level; Module 3 adds the implementation and test tier.

## What this lab does *not* do (in Module 2)

- It does **not** implement the capsule in Python. The function
  harness in [Step 4](../../../../labs/greeting-capsule/walkthrough.html#step-4-implement-the-capability)
  is a course-local teaching convention and is covered by
  Module 3 ("Implement and test a capsule").
- It does **not** compose a Pico or hand-resolve the capability.
  Steps 6 and 7 are covered by Module 4 ("Compose a Pico").
- It does **not** copy the upstream schema into the Academy tree.
  The lab fetches it per-run and reads it from the untracked
  `build/upstream/` directory (memo23 §3.2, memo2 §5 (a)).
